--- Page 1 (Beckerman_95a) --- 1915 Dear Folks, Have just found out what the story is about the increase of allotment that you were telling me about. It seems that there are two kinds of dependents (other than wives): a) Those that depend upon the soldier for chief support. They are supposed to receive more than 50% of their entire income from the soldier. This is called "B-1" dependency and the allotment pays 50 per mo. Thus if Mama were a Class B-1 dependent the soldier gets 50 allot. per mo. b) Those who depend upon the soldier for substantial support but not chief support. (Soldier's contribution more than 50%). The allotment pays about 37 per month. That is what Mama is getting. She is substantial support. --- Page 2 (Beckerman_95b) --- to get into the "B-1" dependency class and get the increased allowance. If there are any further questions please let me know. I have written this rather hurriedly during office hours. Love. Jack. --- Page 3 (Beckerman_95c) --- Every 6 months the office of Dependency Benefits in Newark sends out a form to all class "B" and "B-1" dependents. It is called Form No. W.D.A.C.O. #650. The form is sent out 6 months after the allotment starts and each six months thereafter. Its purpose is to find out whether class "B" dependents will receive their regular class B allotment amount or whether they will jump up to a "B-1" dependency during the succeeding 6 months. The papers are sent out by the office of Dependency Benefits. not by the soldier. These are the papers Sara received. Because of certain answers she indicated on the form they decided that she was now in the "B-1" class and $50.00 to the amount of age 0 and I was not yet a 20 at the time.
